notice: Illustrative lab reference conditions only. Not a CIS or Microsoft certification and not a client-approved benchmark. A Fail is a configuration observation that requires analyst review against the client's approved baseline and documented exceptions before it becomes a finding. Where a value is absent, the rule states explicitly what that absence means; no default is ever assumed silently. Severity is never assigned by this rule set.

rules.title: Domain firewall profile enabled
rules.basis: Microsoft security-baseline review required for the exact OS/build
rules.applicability: Applicable only where the Domain profile exists and the approved baseline expects it enabled.

rules.title: Private firewall profile enabled
rules.basis: Microsoft security-baseline review required for the exact OS/build
rules.applicability: Verify profile use and approved exceptions.

rules.title: Public firewall profile enabled
rules.basis: Microsoft security-baseline review required for the exact OS/build
rules.applicability: Verify profile use and approved exceptions.

rules.title: SMB server configuration disables SMB1
rules.basis: Lab security reference; validate against the applicable Microsoft baseline
rules.applicability: Verify the feature/provider exists on the assessed OS and whether a documented legacy exception applies.

rules.title: SMB server configuration requires signing
rules.basis: Lab reference only; OS/role baseline must be confirmed
rules.applicability: Do not report solely from this rule until the target OS/role and approved baseline are confirmed.

rules.title: SMB client configuration requires signing
rules.basis: Lab reference only; OS/role baseline must be confirmed
rules.applicability: Do not report solely from this rule until the target OS/role and approved baseline are confirmed.

rules.title: NLA configured when RDP connections are enabled
rules.basis: Lab security reference; validate against the exact OS baseline
rules.applicability: Only evaluates the local RDP configuration provider. It does not prove the port is reachable from another network.

rules.title: EnableLUA configured as 1
rules.basis: Lab security reference; validate against the exact OS baseline
rules.applicability: A registry value alone does not establish every UAC-related control or pending-restart state.

rules.title: Built-in local Guest account disabled
rules.basis: Lab security reference; validate against the exact OS baseline
rules.applicability: Not used as a domain-controller directory assessment. The collector selects the built-in local Guest by RID.

rules.title: WDigest does not cache cleartext credentials
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: VERSION DEPENDENT. On Windows 8.1, Server 2012 R2 and later an absent value means cleartext caching is off. On Windows 7, Server 2008 R2, Windows 8 and Server 2012 with KB2871997 installed, an absent value means cleartext caching is ON. Confirm the host version before reading an absent value as safe.

absent_means.interpretation: No value is configured. The effective behaviour depends on the operating system version, so no determination is made here. On Windows 8.1 and later the default is safe; on earlier versions with KB2871997 it is not.

rules.title: LSA runs as a protected process
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: RunAsPPL 1 and 2 both enable LSA protection; 2 is the form without the UEFI variable lock, available on Windows 11 22H2 and later. Either value satisfies this check.

absent_means.interpretation: No LSA protection value is configured, so LSASS is not running as a protected process and its memory is exposed to credential theft tooling.

rules.title: LAN Manager password hashes are not stored
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Applies to all supported Windows versions.

absent_means.interpretation: No value is configured, so LAN Manager hash storage is not explicitly disabled and legacy weak hashes may be retained.

rules.title: Cached interactive logons are limited
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Compare against the client's approved value. A higher count is a configuration observation, not a confirmed exposure; the appropriate number depends on how often the host operates offline.

absent_means.interpretation: No value is present; the effective default cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone.

rules.title: Automatic logon is not configured
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Where automatic logon is enabled, confirm separately whether a password is stored in the registry.

absent_means.interpretation: No automatic-logon value is configured, so interactive authentication is required.

rules.title: No automatic-logon password is stored in the registry
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: The collector records only whether a stored password exists; the value itself is never collected.

rules.title: A local administrator password solution is present on the host
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Presence only. This records that LAPS components or a configuration root exist; it does NOT establish that password backup is configured. CRED08 tests the determining value.

rules.title: LLMNR is disabled by policy
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Disabling LLMNR can affect name resolution on flat networks. Confirm operational impact with the client.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so LLMNR remains enabled by default and the host will respond to multicast name queries, which permits credential relay and spoofing on the local segment.

rules.title: The SMBv1 client driver is disabled
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Complements the server-side SMB1 setting. A start value of 4 is disabled.

absent_means.interpretation: The driver key is not present; the SMBv1 client state cannot be determined from this evidence.

rules.title: Windows Installer does not always install with elevated privileges (machine policy)
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Exploitable only when the matching user-side policy is also enabled. A single side set to 1 is a configuration weakness, not a confirmed escalation path.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so the setting is disabled by default.

rules.title: Windows Installer does not always install with elevated privileges (user policy)
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Reflects the account that performed the collection only, not every user of the host.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured for the collecting account, so the setting is disabled by default.

rules.title: PowerShell script block logging is enabled
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Absence reduces detection and forensic capability. It is not itself an exploitable weakness.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so PowerShell script block logging is not enabled and script execution will not be recorded for investigation.

rules.title: PowerShell module logging is enabled
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Detection capability. Confirm the client's logging strategy before reporting.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so PowerShell module logging is not enabled.

rules.title: Administrator approval mode is enforced for the built-in administrator
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Applies where a built-in administrator account is in use.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so the built-in administrator account operates with a full token and is not subject to User Account Control prompting.

rules.title: Remote local-account access is not exempted from UAC filtering
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: A value of 1 permits local accounts to be used for full-privilege remote administration, which also enables lateral movement between hosts sharing a password.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so remote local-account access remains filtered by default.

rules.title: A minimum local password length is enforced
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Local accounts only; domain policy is not represented in this evidence. The value is parsed from English-language output, so on a non-English host this check must be treated as not tested.

absent_means.interpretation: The policy value could not be read, most likely because the host is not English-language. No determination is made.

rules.title: An account lockout threshold is configured
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Local accounts only. A threshold of 0 disables lockout entirely and is weaker than any positive value, which is why this check declares a range rather than a maximum. Compare the upper bound against the client's approved policy.

absent_means.interpretation: The policy value could not be read. No determination is made.

rules.title: AutoRun is restricted for all drive types
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: 255 disables AutoRun on every drive type. Lower values restrict it partially.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so AutoRun restriction relies on the operating system default and removable media handling is not explicitly controlled.

rules.title: Windows Update source is not an unencrypted server
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Only meaningful when UseWUServer is 1. An update server reached over http allows an attacker on the network path to supply content that installs with SYSTEM privileges. Confirm UseWUServer before reporting.

absent_means.interpretation: No update server is configured, so the host uses Microsoft Update directly and this check does not apply.

rules.title: Update server certificate pinning is not disabled
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Disabling enterprise certificate pinning for update detection reverses a Microsoft hardening measure.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so certificate pinning remains at its default enabled state.

rules.title: Printer driver installation is restricted to administrators
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Microsoft states that no combination of other mitigations is equivalent to this setting. Applies wherever the print spooler is running.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so non-administrators may install printer drivers, which execute with system privileges.

rules.title: Point and Print does not suppress elevation prompts
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: Suppressing the elevation prompt removes the only user-visible control on driver installation.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so the default prompting behaviour applies.

rules.title: Remote management service does not permit unencrypted traffic
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Read together with basic authentication. The two combined place credentials on the wire in clear.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so unencrypted transport is not permitted by default.

rules.title: Remote management service does not permit basic authentication
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Basic authentication transmits credentials in a reversible encoding. Significance depends on whether the transport is encrypted.

absent_means.interpretation: No policy is configured, so basic authentication is not permitted by default.

rules.title: NetBIOS over TCP/IP is disabled on every interface
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Evaluated by the analyst per interface: a NetbiosOptions value of 2 is disabled, while 0 and 1 both leave it enabled. Every interface must be checked, not only the primary one.

absent_means.interpretation: No interface records were read, so no determination is made.

rules.title: Managed local administrator password backup is configured
rules.basis: Microsoft security baseline; confirm against the exact OS build before reporting
rules.applicability: BackupDirectory is the determining value: 1 backs up to Entra ID, 2 to Active Directory. The presence of a configuration root alone does not mean password management is in effect.

absent_means.interpretation: No password backup directory is configured, so local administrator passwords are not being managed or rotated. Where the same password is used across hosts this enables lateral movement, though that reuse is a separate finding requiring its own evidence.

rules.title: Legacy network authentication is not permitted
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Levels 0, 1 and 2 permit LAN Manager or NTLMv1 authentication. An absent value behaves as level 3 on modern Windows, but a domain controller may still accept NTLMv1 from clients.

absent_means.interpretation: No value is configured. The effective level cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone and should be verified against the applicable baseline.

rules.title: PowerShell 7 script block logging is enabled
rules.basis: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark reference; confirm the applicable benchmark level with the client
rules.applicability: Only applicable where PowerShell 7 is installed. Configuring the Windows PowerShell policy root does not configure PowerShell 7.

absent_means.interpretation: No PowerShell 7 policy is configured. Whether that matters depends on whether PowerShell 7 is installed on this host, which the same evidence source records.

rules.title: No saved open network is set to connect automatically
rules.basis: CIS/vendor wireless hardening reference; confirm the applicable benchmark with the client
rules.applicability: Applicable to hosts with a wireless adapter. An open network set to auto-connect lets the host silently join a same-named attacker access point.

rules.title: No saved network uses legacy WPA or WEP encryption
rules.basis: WPA(1)/WEP are deprecated; WPA2 or WPA3 is the accepted baseline
rules.applicability: Applicable to hosts with a wireless adapter. Legacy encryption is broken and exposes the pre-shared key and traffic.

rules.title: No saved network uses the weak TKIP cipher
rules.basis: TKIP is deprecated; CCMP/GCMP (AES) is the accepted baseline
rules.applicability: Applicable to hosts with a wireless adapter. TKIP is cryptographically weak and should not be negotiated.

rules.title: 802.1X wireless profiles validate the authentication server certificate
rules.basis: Enterprise (802.1X) profiles must validate the RADIUS server certificate against a trusted root
rules.applicability: Applicable to hosts with a wireless adapter and 802.1X profiles. Without server-certificate validation a rogue access point can present a fake RADIUS server and harvest domain credentials (evil twin).

rules.title: The currently connected wireless network uses WPA2 or WPA3
rules.basis: An active association should use WPA2 or WPA3, never open or legacy
rules.applicability: Applicable only when the host is currently associated to a wireless network. Not evaluated when disconnected.

rules.title: No open (unencrypted) wireless network is saved
rules.basis: Saved open networks are a standing exposure even when connected manually
rules.applicability: Applicable to hosts with a wireless adapter. A saved open profile can be silently impersonated by an attacker access point.

rules.title: Corporate wireless uses 802.1X rather than only a shared pre-shared key
rules.basis: A WPA2/WPA3-Personal pre-shared key is recoverable from any joined endpoint; corporate wireless should use 802.1X
rules.applicability: Advisory. Flags saved Personal (PSK) networks because the key can be extracted off any endpoint that stored it. Corporate SSIDs should use 802.1X; home or guest networks are expected exceptions the analyst records.

rules.title: The connected wireless network uses management-frame protection (PMF)
rules.basis: 802.11w management-frame protection (mandatory with WPA3) resists deauthentication and management-frame spoofing
rules.applicability: Evaluated only when associated and the AKM suite can be read. Absence of PMF permits deauthentication and management-frame attacks that assist evil-twin and denial conditions.

control_baseline.notice: Baseline control references only. They identify which control family a check relates to; they are not a certification and they do not assert that the control as a whole is met. Engagement-specific frameworks are added through an overlay file rather than being written into this profile, so one client's framework never becomes every client's. Control identifiers for frameworks that are not public - a client's own benchmark, or a proprietary control-numbering scheme - must be transcribed from the framework document by an assessor and are deliberately not guessed here.
